children: stock gained more than 2% in Thursday premarket trading after rising more than 5% Wednesday, as investors looked ahead to a potentially important milestone: Starship's first orbital test on September 22.
The 14th Starship flight is expected to send the vehicle into orbit around Earth and deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites, tying the launch directly to one of SpaceX's biggest growth businesses.
CEO Elon Musk has said Starlink V3 deployment will begin in September and that the next-generation satellites could eventually deliver more than 100 times the bandwidth of the current constellation.
That makes the upcoming test about more than launch technology.

Cathie Wood has said each Starship launch could potentially generate $1 billion in revenue, while several Wall Street analysts increasingly view Starship reusability as critical to expanding SpaceX's long-term opportunity in connectivity and orbital computing.

Morgan Stanley analyst Adam Jonas recently reiterated a Buy rating and $300 price target, implying roughly 99% upside from current levels. Jonas believes SpaceX's AI business and orbital computing opportunity are not fully reflected in the valuation.
Bernstein analyst Douglas Harned also maintained an Outperform rating with a $248 target, implying about 64% upside.
"Most important for SpaceX's valuation remains gaining Starship reusability to enable orbital data centers," Harned said.
He expects SpaceX's Connectivity business to generate more than $100 billion in EBITDA by 2031 and sees additional upside from a potential Starlink mobile virtual network operator strategy.
William Blair analyst Louis DiPalma is also constructive after another large AI-compute agreement.
"Last night's deal is SpaceXAI's fourth compute agreement in the past four months that is greater than $11 billion in ARR," DiPalma said.
The Sept. 22 flight could become a major proof point.
A successful orbital mission and Starlink V3 deployment would strengthen the case that Starship is moving closer to becoming a commercial platform rather than simply an experimental launch system.
The bigger valuation question is whether reusability can materially lower launch costs and unlock the orbital-data-center opportunity analysts increasingly cite.
Wall Street's average SpaceX price target stands at $232.07, implying about 54% upside.

The risk is equally clear: much of that upside depends on execution. Delays, failed tests or slower Starship reusability progress could push back the timelines behind some of the most ambitious valuation assumptions.

title: Morgan Stanley Sees 99% Upside in SpaceX Stock
